question: According to the lecturer, what are the three conditions of 'istita'ah' (ability) that make Hajj mandatory on a person?

initial_retrieved.text: And there's another narration which we have already covered before, and I'm going to show you that today as well. So, Hajj is mandatory for those who are able to go, who have istita'ah. What does that mean? It has three understandings based: first one, when a person has the travel expenses, when a person is able to travel, then he is capable to go for Hajj. And also this person should have enough expenses for the people he's leaving behind.

Let's just talk about a few things we have already covered yesterday. I'm just going to quickly go over them, just jot down the title parts, right? Just know the main headings, Insha'Allah. Hajj is an obligation, and it's a very important obligation, it's a command of Allah, and also Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, he emphasized it. And if a person wants to perform more Hajj, they can, and Insha'Allah we will cover that narration in a bit as well. And don't delay Hajj if Allah has given you enough, and if you fulfill all three conditions of istita'ah, then Insha'Allah go and don't delay it for petty reasons or for worldly reasons. And once Hajj becomes an obligation, do it before anything else.

So, what's the proof that Hajj is mandatory for those who are able to go? He was given khutbah and he said: 'O people, Allah has made Hajj an obligation for you, so perform Hajj.' Thereupon a person said, 'Is it to be performed every year?' Rasulullah Sallallahu Alayhi wa Sallam, he kept quiet, but this person repeated his question three times.

We are going to talk about the ability, we are going to talk about what is istita'ah in a bit.

So, scholars have mentioned in the tafaseer: safe way, when a person's life and property is safe, then it's okay for us to go. But if it's not safe, then it's not mandatory for us to go that year if there's a problem. So, Alhamdulillah because of this opinion, the COVID years were okay for us if we were not able to go, because it wasn't safe for our life, isn't it, SubhanAllah? And if people were not called for Hajj or they were not allowed to go for Hajj or Umrah, then it wasn't something so bad, it's totally allowed based on all of these narrations. And then if a person is not physically able to go, then again that person is not required to go. So, physical capability is also one of the conditions.

And Hajj is a very important pillar of our deen. Let's talk about the importance of Hajj. First of all, why is it important? Because it's a command of Allah, that's why it's important. It is called the rope of Islam, strong bond of Islam—that's why it's important. Let's look at this beautiful narration about rope of Islam or strong bond of Islam: Sahaba mentioned that we were sitting with Rasulullah, so one of them mentioned that we were sitting with Rasulullah and he asked: 'Which bond of Islam is the strongest?' So, this means this person is rich enough to go for Hajj, because that person has money to go for Hajj and also his family is not going to suffer. Second point: that it should be safe, it should be safe to go.

But there is something to remember: this person believes that Hajj is fard, but not going because of laziness, because of whatever. But believing that Hajj is not mandatory or Hajj is not part of Islam makes a person a non-believer, kicks a person out of the fold of Islam. So, it's something which is very important to remember.

question: According to the lecturer, what are the first four points given to explain why Makkah is a place of safety and security?
rewritten_query: According to the lecturer, what are the first four points given to explain why Makkah is a place of safety and security?

initial_retrieved.text: And Amna is security. How is Makkah a place of safety and security? We're going to cover six points, but I really want all of you to jot down only the four points first—the first four points only at this point, because we are going to touch the other points if you get a chance in this course. First point: sacred place till Qiyamah. Makkah is going to stay sacred till Qiyamah; we need to remember that it's a sanctuary till the Day of Resurrection. Rasulullah, he said that on the day of conquest of Makkah:

First, SubhanAllah. And then fourth point: safety from Dajjal's fitna. We all are scared about Dajjal, isn't it? So, SubhanAllah Makkah is safe from Dajjal, Masjid al-Haram is safe from Dajjal.
